question: For a fixed centered full-dimensional rational polytope P with the origin in its interior, when does there exist a full-rank lattice M with Vert(P) subset M and Vert(P^o) subset M* under the declared dot pairing, and what is the minimal such M?
level: Adva research terminology and external exact rational arithmetic; no stable semantic operation, no new vocabulary name

criterion.name: minimal-lattice lemma
criterion.statement: Such an M exists if and only if every pairing dot(v,y) with a supplied primal vertex v and a computed polar vertex y is an integer. The minimal candidate is M = Z-span(Vert(P)); no larger lattice can be easier, because M1 subset M2 implies M2* subset M1*.
criterion.consequence: The question is decided by one finite pairing check over the two vertex lists. No lattice search is performed and no enumeration of lattices is claimed.

objects: sheared_cube_3d: A(x,y,z)=(x+y,y,z) applied to the cube vertices
to24_3d: signed permutations of (0,1,2), equivalently |x_i|<=2 and |x_1|+|x_2|+|x_3|<=3
unimodular_image_of_to24_3d: the same A applied to the TO24 vertices
twice_to24_3d: the TO24 vertex set scaled by 2

types.coordinates: Q^d with exact Fraction, d in {2,3}
types.origin: (0,...,0), fixed and required to be interior
types.pairing: standard dot product between declared primal and dual coordinate spaces
types.polar: P^o={y: dot(v,y)<=1 for every supplied primal vertex v}, vertices by complete active-constraint enumeration
types.minimal_lattice: M = Z-span(Vert(P)), reported by a Hermite basis and its index in Z^d

quantifiers: Every d-subset of each frozen vertex list, for each computed polar
Every primal-polar vertex pairing in each fixture
The existence question quantifies over every compatible full-rank lattice, discharged by the lemma's two directions rather than by a search
assumptions: Classical polar duality for full-dimensional compact convex polytopes with interior origin
Classical lattices: M full rank in Q^d, M*=Hom(M,Z) under the declared pairing
The self-contained checker is an external mathematical oracle, not the Rust semantic kernel
Batyrev reflexivity and Calabi-Yau mirror symmetry motivate the question only; no construction is attempted
protected: Q4/M6 typed histories and unfilled boundaries remain unchanged
The fixed centered TO24 obstruction from the 2026-09-10 record is extended, not reinterpreted
Pascal-rooted growth obligation remains Open; no geometry catalog admission
No group quotient, metric refinement, crepant subdivision or mirror constructed
acceptance: The square, the reflexive triangle, the cube, the sheared cube and the reflexive simplex satisfy the criterion
TO24, its unimodular image and twice TO24 fail it, each with an explicit nonintegral pairing certificate
The computed polar of the sheared cube equals the contragredient transport of the unsheared polar, and applying A instead of A^(-T) is refused
Every fixture whose facets are declared also matches the normals/offsets reading, and the offset set is reported
A forged polar vertex, an epsilon-integrality shortcut, incomplete coverage, a non-full-dimensional domain, a boundary origin and a wrong dual transport are each refused
unknown: Budget or required evidence unavailable; partial enumeration is never promoted, and a refused shortcut is reported as a refusal, not as evidence
